text: What does Sensei actually see? A mentor learns by watching the work, so it’s fair to ask what it watches, and where that goes.
Point it at a folder once and it stays up to date by itself. It watches your folders, your git history, every assistant session, and what each session used: tokens, cost, context.
A session arrives as events: a prompt, a tool call, a result. Sensei turns them into one record: how long it took, whether it landed first time, and what it cost.
It also maps the code itself: files, symbols, calls and docs. When a file changes, only its part of the map is updated.
All of it stays on your machine. Secrets are blacked out the moment they’re captured, before anything is stored.
Sharing with your team is your choice. You see exactly what would leave, anonymised, and nothing goes until you confirm.
Sensei. It sees the work. You keep it.
